questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: The 'Spatial Organisation' approach in human geography, which utilized computer cartography and universal physics-based models, emerged prominently during which era?
options: A) Late 1950s to late 1960s
B) Early colonial period
C) Inter-war period of the 1930s
D) Post-modern phase of the 1990s
questions.explanation: During the late 1950s to late 1960s, spatial analysis and quantitative revolution dominated human geography, replacing descriptive regional approaches with quantitative laws.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: The 'Behavioural School' of thought in human geography laid great emphasis on:
options: A) Deterministic control of human destiny by local climate alone
B) Lived human experience, perception of space, and social categories like ethnicity, race, and religion
C) Mechanical profit maximization under perfect mathematical markets
D) Exclusive study of geomorphological landforms without human presence
questions.explanation: The Behavioural school shifted focus to cognitive perception, mental maps, and lived human experiences across diverse ethnic and religious groups.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: In the population theory of Thomas Malthus, 'positive checks' that restore the balance between population and food supply include:
options: A) Moral restraint and celibacy
B) Postponement of marriage
C) Famines, epidemics, wars, and natural calamities
D) Adoption of modern family planning techniques
questions.explanation: Malthus identified two checks: preventive checks (moral restraint, celibacy, late marriage) and positive checks (famines, plagues, wars, diseases).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: While it took more than 300 years for the human population to grow from 500 million to 1 billion, how long did it take to double from 3 billion to 6 billion in the 20th century?
options: A) Over 150 years
B) Approximately 90 years
C) Barely 10 years
D) Approximately 40 years
questions.explanation: Human population surged from 3 billion in 1960 to 6 billion in 1999—a doubling time of just about 40 years due to the precipitous decline in death rates.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: In population geography, the 'Dependency Ratio' is calculated as the ratio of:
options: A) Dependent population (aged 0-14 and 65+) to working-age population (aged 15-64)
B) Rural population to total urban metropolitan population
C) Total unemployed males to total registered wage earners
D) Number of live births to total maternal mortality cases
questions.explanation: The dependency ratio measures the demographic burden placed on the economically active working-age cohort (15–64 years) by dependent children (0–14) and elderly (65+).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: The 'Welfare Approach' to human development views human beings primarily as:
options: A) Autonomous agents capable of transforming political structures
B) Beneficiaries of government developmental expenditure on education, health, and social amenities
C) Units of industrial labor input in production functions
D) Consumers whose value is measured solely by private wealth
questions.explanation: The Welfare approach treats humans as passive recipients or beneficiaries, advocating higher government expenditure on health, education, and amenities.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: Which of the following small island developing nations has consistently achieved a higher HDI ranking than many larger, richer nations due to long-term state investments in healthcare and education?
options: A) Papua New Guinea
B) Madagascar
C) Sri Lanka
D) Haiti
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka (along with Kerala within India) is cited in NCERT as a classic example of a developing territory achieving high human development despite modest per capita income.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: In the human development paradigm, 'Productivity' refers specifically to:
options: A) Maximizing automated robotic output in heavy assembly lines
B) Extracting non-renewable mineral resources at maximum speed
C) Increasing total agricultural acreage through deforestation
D) Human labour productivity enhanced through investments in education, health, and capability building
questions.explanation: Productivity in human development refers to human labor productivity; people must be built into productive agents through continuous investments in their health and capabilities.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Why does extensive commercial grain farming in the temperate grasslands (Prairies, Steppes, Pampas) exhibit low yield per hectare but very high yield per worker?
options: A) Farms are exceptionally large and completely mechanised, requiring very few human labourers relative to the immense land area
B) Soils are extremely infertile and require continuous manual weeding by migrant peasants
C) Severe tropical droughts destroy half the standing crop every season
D) Governments legally restrict the use of all motorized machinery on grain farms
questions.explanation: Extensive commercial grain farming operates on massive holdings (hundreds of hectares) using combine harvesters and tractors, so output per worker is huge, though per-hectare yield is lower than intensive farming.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Which specialized branch of Mediterranean agriculture involves the cultivation of grapes for making high-grade wines and raisins?
options: A) Sericulture
B) Viticulture
C) Pisciculture
D) Floriculture
questions.explanation: Viticulture is the cultivation of grapevines; the best-quality grapes are processed into distinctive regional wines, while inferior grapes are dried into raisins and currants.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Quinine, a vital medicinal drug historically extracted from the bark of which tree, is an example of a forest gathering product?
options: A) Zapote tree
B) Eucalyptus tree
C) Cinchona tree
D) Rubber tree
questions.explanation: Quinine, extracted from the dried bark of the cinchona tree native to the tropical Andes and Amazon rainforest, has been used for centuries to treat malaria.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: In which region of Europe has market gardening under artificial glasshouses and heated greenhouses developed into a major high-tech agribusiness?
options: A) Northern Scandinavia
B) The Balkan highlands
C) The Iberian drylands
D) The Netherlands
questions.explanation: The Netherlands is world-renowned for intensive horticultural production of tulips and vegetables cultivated in heated, computer-controlled glasshouses.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Which of the following is a key operational characteristic of 'Footloose Industries'?
options: A) They are largely non-polluting and can be located in diverse locations accessible by road transport
B) They must be located directly at coal pitheads due to massive weight loss
C) They require hundreds of acres of water bodies for barge transport
D) They rely exclusively on child labor in unorganized cottage workshops
questions.explanation: Footloose industries use standardized components, produce light products with negligible transport costs, cause little pollution, and depend primarily on road accessibility.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Silicon Glen, a renowned technopolis region specializing in computer manufacturing and electronics engineering, is located in:
options: A) Bavaria (Germany)
B) Scotland (United Kingdom)
C) Lombardy (Italy)
D) Catalonia (Spain)
questions.explanation: Silicon Glen refers to the concentration of high-tech electronics, semiconductor, and computer enterprises situated in the central belt of Scotland.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Petrochemical industries are typically situated near oil refineries or coastal ports primarily because:
options: A) They require high atmospheric humidity to prevent nuclear reactions
B) They must use sea water to wash cotton fibres
C) They utilize raw petroleum by-products (naphtha, ethane, propane) that are hazardous and bulky to transport over long distances
D) They are strictly banned from operating on dry continental landmasses
questions.explanation: Petrochemical plants process refinery fractions (naphtha, cracking gases) into plastics, polymers, and synthetic fibres, making proximity to refineries or crude terminals optimal.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: In the geography of trade and settlements, the 'Threshold Population' of a central place refers to:
options: A) The maximum distance a customer is willing to travel to purchase a commodity
B) The total number of retired elderly residents in an urban block
C) The statutory population cap established by municipal election laws
D) The minimum number of consumers required to support the economic viability of a particular service or store
questions.explanation: Threshold population is the minimum population size needed to sustain a given business, store, or public facility economically.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Which retail format purchases merchandise in large volumes directly from manufacturers and operates multiple retail stores with uniform design across various cities?
options: A) Chain stores
B) Periodic weekly markets
C) Village hawker stalls
D) Artisan household guilds
questions.explanation: Chain stores operate multiple branches under common ownership, standardizing procurement and passing economies of scale to consumers.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Which of the following professional roles is classified under 'Quinary Activities'?
options: A) Hospital nurses dispensing daily medications
B) Senior policy advisors and strategic government executives drafting national legislation
C) Bus drivers navigating urban transit routes
D) Supermarket cashiers scanning grocery barcodes
questions.explanation: Quinary activities encompass the highest levels of strategic decision-making, formulation of public policy, and top-tier scientific evaluation ('gold-collar' workers).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: The North Pacific Sea Route facilitates heavy commercial maritime traffic connecting the west coast ports of North America (Vancouver, Seattle, San Francisco) with:
options: A) West African ports including Lagos, Luanda, and Dakar
B) South American Atlantic ports including Santos and Buenos Aires
C) East Asian ports including Yokohama, Kobe, Shanghai, and Hong Kong
D) Mediterranean ports including Genoa, Marseille, and Alexandria
questions.explanation: The North Pacific route traverses the northern Pacific basin along the Great Circle route connecting North America's west coast with East and Southeast Asia.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: The Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline) was engineered to transport crude oil from oilfields in Saudi Arabia directly to the port terminal of:
options: A) Aden on the Arabian Sea
B) Basra on the Persian Gulf
C) Suez on the Red Sea
D) Sidon on the Mediterranean coast
questions.explanation: The 1,214 km Tapline delivered crude oil from Saudi fields directly to the Mediterranean port of Sidon in Lebanon, avoiding the Suez transit.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: A situation where a country's total value of merchandise exports exceeds its total value of merchandise imports is termed:
options: A) Favourable balance of trade
B) Unfavourable balance of trade
C) Negative balance of payments
D) Customs tariff deficit
questions.explanation: A positive or favourable balance of trade occurs when the total value of a nation's exports exceeds the value of its imports.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: A major criticism levied by developing nations against the World Trade Organisation (WTO) is that:
options: A) The WTO strictly forbids all international cargo shipping on high seas
B) Influential developed nations maintain domestic agricultural subsidies while forcing developing countries to open their markets
C) The WTO mandates that all member nations must adopt a single universal paper currency
D) The WTO requires all member states to dissolve their sovereign armed forces
questions.explanation: Developing countries argue that Western nations protect their farmers with huge subsidies while demanding tariff cuts from poor countries, creating unfair competition.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - People
questions.question: According to the 2011 Census of India, which state recorded a negative decadal population growth rate (-0.58%) between 2001 and 2011?
options: A) Kerala
B) Goa
C) Nagaland
D) Sikkim
questions.explanation: Nagaland was the only Indian state to register a negative population growth rate (-0.58%) in the 2001–2011 census decade, after an inflated base count in 2001.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - People
questions.question: The Sino-Tibetan (Kirata) language family in India accounts for less than 1% of the total population and is spoken primarily in:
options: A) The Malabar coastal belt of Kerala
B) The Chota Nagpur plateau of Jharkhand
C) The coastal plains of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh
D) Himalayan regions of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and the North-Eastern states
questions.explanation: Sino-Tibetan languages (Bodo, Mizo, Manipuri, Garo, Ladakhi) are spoken by indigenous communities along the Himalayan borderlands and the Northeast.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - People
questions.question: In the Census of India, an individual who worked for less than 183 days (six months) during the reference year is designated as a:
options: A) Marginal worker
B) Main worker
C) Non-worker
D) Permanent employee
questions.explanation: Marginal workers are individuals who participated in productive economic work for fewer than 183 days during the preceding twelve months.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Human Settlements
questions.question: In Indian urban census classification, an urban settlement having a population between 1 million and 5 million (10 lakh to 50 lakh) is designated as a:
options: A) Megacity
B) Metropolitan city
C) Class IV town
D) Census outpost
questions.explanation: Indian census classifies towns with 1 to 5 million people as metropolitan cities, and urban agglomerations exceeding 5 million as mega cities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Human Settlements
questions.question: Singrauli and Kothagudem are functionally classified in India as:
options: A) Tourist hill stations
B) Administrative capitals
C) Mining towns
D) Port gateway cities
questions.explanation: Singrauli (MP) and Kothagudem (Telangana) developed as major urban settlements around extensive coal extraction and mining operations.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Human Settlements
questions.question: In the flood-prone lower Ganga plains of West Bengal and eastern Bihar, rural settlements are predominantly clustered on:
options: A) Deep marshy depressions within stagnant swamp backwaters
B) Dry sand dunes in rain shadow deserts
C) Subterranean limestone sinkholes
D) Elevated natural river levees and river bluffs above seasonal flood levels
questions.explanation: In deltaic and alluvial floodplains, houses cluster on natural levees (dry points) to protect lives and property from recurrent monsoon floods.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Common Property Resources (CPRs) in rural India are especially vital for the livelihood of landless households and small farmers because they provide:
options: A) Free access to animal fodder, domestic fuel wood, medicinal herbs, and grazing lands
B) Exclusive private mineral extraction licenses for export
C) Direct government cash deposits from international trade royalties
D) Commercial cellular telecommunication towers on private farmland
questions.explanation: CPRs (village pastures, community forests, threshing grounds) provide sustenance resources—especially fodder for cattle and firewood—crucial for marginal and landless rural families.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In West Bengal, farmers cultivate three distinct seasonal crops of rice in an agricultural year, which are locally known as:
options: A) Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid
B) Aus, Aman, and Boro
C) Jhum, Milpa, and Ladang
D) Aus, Gram, and Tur
questions.explanation: Due to warm temperatures and abundant water, farmers in West Bengal, Assam, and coastal Odisha grow three rice crops: Aus (autumn), Aman (winter), and Boro (summer).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Which Indian state is the foremost producer of Groundnut, accounting for over one-third of the country's total output?
options: A) Punjab
B) Assam
C) Gujarat
D) West Bengal
questions.explanation: Gujarat is the leading groundnut producing state in India, where the crop thrives in the semi-arid, well-drained sandy loams of Saurashtra.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Rapeseed and Mustard are cool-season oilseed crops cultivated primarily during which cropping season in northern India?
options: A) Kharif season
B) Zaid season
C) Monsoon season
D) Rabi season
questions.explanation: Rapeseed and mustard are temperate rabi crops sown in October–November and harvested in February–March; Rajasthan is the leading producer.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In Rajasthan and Maharashtra, excessive withdrawal of groundwater has resulted in an alarming increase in the concentration of which toxic chemical element in drinking water?
options: A) Fluoride
B) Chlorine
C) Sodium
D) Helium
questions.explanation: Depletion of deep groundwater tables exposes fluoride-bearing rocks, leaching dangerous concentrations of fluoride into drinking water and causing skeletal fluorosis.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The 'North-Eastern Plateau Belt' is India's richest mineral region, encompassing the Chota Nagpur, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh plateaus, and contains rich reserves of:
options: A) Crude petroleum, natural gas, and rock salt only
B) Iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite, and mica
C) Monazite sands and coastal heavy ilmenite only
D) Precious diamonds and native gold veins exclusively
questions.explanation: The North-Eastern Plateau belt covers Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal, hosting premier Gondwana coalfields, rich haematite iron ore, manganese, bauxite, and mica.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO) operates one of Asia's largest integrated alumina refineries at Damanjodi, which is linked directly to bauxite mines at:
options: A) Khetri in Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan
B) Kallakkurichi in Viluppuram district, Tamil Nadu
C) Panchpatmali in Koraput district, Odisha
D) Puga Valley in Ladakh
questions.explanation: NALCO's Damanjodi alumina refinery in Koraput, Odisha, is supplied by automated cable conveyor from the open-cast Panchpatmali bauxite mine.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Unlike peninsular Gondwana coal, 'Tertiary Coal' in India is characterized by high sulphur content and is found in the extra-peninsular rock strata of:
options: A) Damodar valley (Raniganj and Jharia)
B) Mahanadi valley (Talcher)
C) Godavari valley (Singareni)
D) Assam (Makum), Meghalaya (Cherrapunji), and Arunachal Pradesh
questions.explanation: Tertiary coal occurs in the northeastern states (Makum and Nazira in Assam, Cherrapunji and Daranggiri in Meghalaya) and has high sulphur and volatile content.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In India, the most promising oceanic sites identified for generating commercial tidal power through high tidal ranges are situated in:
options: A) The Gulf of Khambhat and the Gulf of Kachchh in Gujarat
B) The Palk Strait between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka
C) The Chilika Lagoon in Odisha
D) The Sunderbans delta mouth along West Bengal
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Khambhat and Gulf of Kachchh exhibit oceanic tidal variations of 8 to 11 metres, providing the highest commercial tidal energy potential in India.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Besides Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh, another prominent experimental geothermal energy site located in an active hot spring zone in India is:
options: A) Durgapur in West Bengal
B) Puga Valley in Ladakh
C) Korba in Chhattisgarh
D) Barauni in Bihar
questions.explanation: Puga Valley in the Changthang region of Ladakh exhibits extensive hot springs and mud pools, selected by the Geological Survey of India for geothermal energy generation.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The Bharmaur region, designated under the Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP), is geographically situated in the basin of which Himalayan river?
options: A) Chenab river
B) Yamuna river
C) Ravi river
D) Satluj river
questions.explanation: Bharmaur is an isolated mountainous tehsil in Chamba district, Himachal Pradesh, situated along the upper catchment of the Ravi river and surrounded by the Pir Panjal range.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In the Indira Gandhi Canal command area, the introduction of perennial canal irrigation initially led to a spectacular increase in cultivated area, but subsequently triggered severe ecological degradation in the form of:
options: A) Permanent permafrost freezing of desert sands
B) Severe tectonic sinkholes engulfing villages
C) Massive soil acidification caused by acid volcanic ash
D) Waterlogging and soil salinisation due to excessive water application without subsurface drainage
questions.explanation: Over-irrigation in flat desert terrain underlain by an impermeable gypsum layer caused water tables to rise within 1–2 metres of the surface, creating severe waterlogging and salinisation.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: National Waterway 3 (NW-3) in Kerala comprises a total navigable length of 205 km consisting of the West Coast Canal along with which two industrial branch canals?
options: A) Udyogmandal Canal and Champakkara Canal
B) Buckingham Canal and Commamur Canal
C) Sutlej-Yamuna Link Canal and Sirhind Canal
D) Taldanda Canal and Kendrapara Canal
questions.explanation: NW-3 extends from Kottapuram to Kollam (168 km) along with the Champakkara canal (14 km) and Udyogmandal canal (23 km), running through backwaters.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: Paradip Port, a major deep-water seaport situated in Odisha on the Mahanadi river delta, was constructed primarily to facilitate the export of:
options: A) Automobile components to European assembly plants
B) Iron ore from the mines of Odisha and Jharkhand to overseas markets
C) Raw cotton textiles to Southeast Asian factories
D) Refined petroleum fuels from Middle Eastern terminals
questions.explanation: Paradip Port was developed in Odisha with a deep draft to handle bulk iron ore carriers exporting ore from Kendujhar, Mayurbhanj, and Daitari mines to Japan.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: Haldia Port, situated on the lower Hooghly river estuary, was developed specifically to:
options: A) Serve as India's primary naval submarine combat base
B) Handle international commercial supersonic passenger aviation
C) Relieve severe navigational congestion and draft limitations at the riverine Kolkata Port
D) Divert all iron ore shipments away from Visakhapatnam
questions.explanation: Due to heavy siltation and limited draft in the Hooghly river at Kolkata, Haldia Port was built 105 km downstream to handle large ocean vessels and container freight.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues
questions.question: Along the course of the River Ganga, the industrial city of Kanpur is recognized as a major pollution hotspot primarily due to the discharge of toxic chromium-laden effluents from:
options: A) Offshore petroleum drilling platforms
B) Heavy commercial shipbreaking yards
C) High-altitude copper smelting foundries
D) Leather tanneries and chemical textile processing units
questions.explanation: Kanpur's hundreds of leather tanneries and chemical units historically discharged untreated effluents containing toxic hexavalent chromium and organic waste directly into the Ganga.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues
questions.question: According to census surveys, which of the following is the single largest factor driving the rapid growth of slums in Indian metropolitan cities?
options: A) High influx of rural-to-urban migrants coupled with severe lack of affordable formal housing
B) Government decrees forcing all rural farmers to abandon agriculture
C) Excessive availability of free luxury municipal apartments
D) Rapid closure of all manufacturing industries in suburban centers
questions.explanation: Poverty and lack of employment in rural areas push migrants into cities, where high real estate costs force them to settle in unauthorized, informal slum colonies.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues
questions.question: Soil alkalisation and salinisation in arid and semi-arid irrigated tracts occur primarily through which physical process?
options: A) Subsurface tectonic earthquakes pulverizing rock into sodium carbonate crystals
B) Capillary action drawing dissolved subterranean mineral salts to the topsoil during intense surface evaporation
C) Massive chemical volcanic ash fallout covering net sown fields
D) Continuous acid rain leaching all bases out of the topsoil horizon
questions.explanation: High water tables caused by canal seepage combined with rapid surface evaporation cause capillary rise of saline water, leaving a crust of white salts (reh/kallar) on topsoil.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Establishments that assemble consumer electronic gadgets and semiconductors in pristine, dust-free facilities are commonly described as:
options: A) Heavy smoke-stack industries
B) Basic metallurgical blast furnaces
C) Clean-room manufacturing industries
D) Artisan handloom workshops
questions.explanation: High-tech electronics and semiconductor fabrication require ultra-pure, micro-filtered environments known as clean rooms to prevent airborne particle contamination.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Which of the following sets of crops is harvested during the Rabi agricultural season in northern India?
options: A) Rice, jute, cotton, and bajra
B) Watermelon, cucumber, and fodder crops
C) Tea, coffee, rubber, and cardamom
D) Wheat, gram, barley, and mustard
questions.explanation: Wheat, gram, barley, and mustard are the principal winter (Rabi) crops sown in October–December and harvested in March–April.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: Radio broadcasting in India commenced in 1923 under which pioneering organisation before being converted into All India Radio in 1936?
options: A) Radio Club of Bombay
B) Doordarshan Kendra
C) Prasar Bharati Corporation
D) Bengal Postal Telegraph Union
questions.explanation: Radio broadcasting began in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay, and in 1936 it was formally designated as All India Radio (Akashvani).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO), established in May 1960 to accelerate strategic border infrastructure, constructed the iconic 9.02 km long 'Atal Tunnel' beneath which Himalayan pass?
options: A) Zoji La on the Great Himalayan range
B) Rohtang Pass on the Pir Panjal range
C) Nathu La on the Sikkim border
D) Shipki La on the Indo-Tibetan border
questions.explanation: Atal Tunnel (9.02 km), connecting Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley throughout the year, was constructed by the BRO under Rohtang Pass on the Pir Panjal range.
